title: Stable global consumer confidence masks a present-purchase and investment shortfall beneath stronger expectations and job sentiment
source_unit: Ipsos Global Consumer Confidence Index, September 2026 monthly survey
geography: 30 countries; more than 21,000 adults under age 75 surveyed August 21-September 4, 2026

observations.period: September 2026; global consumer-confidence index and four sub-indices

denominator.unit: countries in Ipsos Global Advisor monthly survey

overall_index.value: Global Consumer Confidence Index is 48.4 and unchanged from August

observations.method: Ipsos monthly online Global Advisor survey of more than 21,000 adults under 75 in 30 countries; the overall index is the average of surveyed countries' National indices and is not a population-weighted global respondent estimate.
observations.uncertainty: Country online samples, index construction, country composition, field timing, and the distinction between perceptions and realized purchasing or employment conditions limit causal or global-welfare interpretation.
observations.subgroup: Country markets, current-purchase perceptions, investment perceptions, future expectations, and job-security perceptions; no single same-household longitudinal pathway is reported here.
observations.counterinterpretation: The gap between sub-indices may reflect question wording or seasonal and country-composition effects rather than a stable psychological split between future hope and present constraint; jobs sentiment is not realized employment security.

observations.period: September 2026; country dispersion and geopolitical aftereffect

high_low_range.value: India has the highest National Index at 66.9, while Türkiye is lowest at 35.3; Japan is 39.4 and Argentina 37.8

thresholds.value: India and Sweden are at or above 60; twelve additional countries are at or above 50; three are below 40

geopolitical_persistence.value: Sentiment remains significantly below its pre-war level in 13 countries and more than one point below its level before the start of the Iran war

monthly_movement.value: Four countries show significant gains, while Malaysia is the only country with a notable decline

observations.method: Ipsos cross-country index comparison using the September 2026 monthly wave and its historical country series.
observations.uncertainty: The release does not identify the causal contribution of war, inflation, domestic politics, or other shocks to country movements; cross-country index levels are not directly comparable measures of household material welfare.
observations.subgroup: 30 national markets, with regional contrasts across Europe and Asia-Pacific and country-specific movements.
observations.counterinterpretation: A lower index can reflect expectations, political mood, or survey response style rather than actual consumption decline; a national average can hide large income, age, and place differences.

broad_loss_absence.value: No country shows significant losses of at least two points across all four sub-indices

broad_gain.value: Chile and Israel show significant month-over-month gains across all four sub-indices

interpretation.value: Aggregate stability coexists with distinct combinations of current constraint, investment caution, future expectation, and job sentiment

observations.method: Comparison of month-over-month changes in Ipsos Current, Investment, Expectations, and Jobs sub-indices.
observations.uncertainty: The source reports index movement rather than household spending, investment, employment, or welfare outcomes; the causal meaning of a multi-index movement remains open.
observations.subgroup: Countries and four sentiment dimensions; it does not identify individual-level transitions among consumers.
observations.counterinterpretation: Multi-index stability or gains may be temporary and may not translate into behavior; country-specific conflict or policy context can make the same index movement mean different things.

related_sources.claim: Prior Ipsos wave referenced by the September release for month-over-month context.

boundary: This record identifies a cross-country consumer-sentiment and sub-index asymmetry. It does not establish realized spending, investment, jobs, household welfare, causal geopolitical effects, or a population-weighted global confidence level.
